sample_unit: mothers of children aged 0-12 months (Phase 1 n=10, Phase 2 n=100)

links.outcome: Value of responsive feedback approach in chatbot design and implementation for tool efficacy
links.effect: Authors conclude the responsive feedback approach improved the efficacy of the digital tool; 80% of users replied at least once and 64% engaged with a nurse. No comparator was used.
links.quote: The study shows the value of using the responsive feedback approach in the chatbot design and implementation to improve the efficacy of the digital tool.

unlisted_practices: Using a nurse-staffed escalation channel for free-form messages that go beyond automated chatbot content
Using a persona-based chatbot to give mothers private, age-appropriate nutrition counseling

screen.reason: Evaluated a conversational counseling chatbot (Poshan Didi) deployed in rural India to mothers, including escalation to nurses, assessing feasibility and engagement rather than testing a specific safeguard intervention.
